narrative.overview:
BetsuBetsu evokes the tactile intimacy and quiet precision of a Japanese restaurant slip printed on thermal paper. It is grounded in the tradition of betsu-betsu (paying separately), transforming the friction of bill calculation into an honest, tangible ritual. The aesthetic avoids cold corporate SaaS tropes and gaudy fintech gradients, choosing instead warm washi paper backgrounds, deep sumi charcoal ink, tactile paper creases, and perforated ticket details.

The density is calibrated for hurried tabletop ergonomics on mobile screens under restaurant lighting. Financial data is displayed with ledger-like rigor: monospace tabular figures ensure numbers align down columns, while delicate paper-crease dividers demarcate stages. Color is applied with intentional restraint—deep charcoal and paper hues carry the structural weight, while scarlet hanko stamps and matcha seals signify verification and mathematical closure.
keyCharacteristics: Tactile Paper Materiality: Natural washi tone (#FAF7F2) paired with pure paper cards (#FFFFFF) and muted parchment (#F3ECE1).
Sumi & Hanko Palette: Rich charcoal typography punctuated by red stamp alerts and green balance seals.
Ledger Monospace Rigor: Tabular numerals for monetary totals, quantities, and audit lines.
Strictly Flat Physicality: Depth conveyed through 1px paper borders (#E5DDCF) and background shifts rather than drop shadows.
Restaurant Ergonomics: High touch contrast, one-handed mobile action buttons, and clear step-based flow.

rules.name: The Hanko Stamp Rule
rules.body: Accent red (#C53030) and matcha green (#1B6B38) are reserved exclusively for mathematical verification, errors, and reconciliation stamps. They never appear as decorative flourishes.

rules.name: The Paper Tone Rule
rules.body: Contrast is created strictly between Washi Cream (#FAF7F2), Pure Parchment (#FFFFFF), and Muted Parchment (#F3ECE1). Never introduce cool grays or blue-tinted slates into the surface hierarchy.

rules.name: The Tabular Numerals Rule
rules.body: Every monetary value, unit price, quantity, tax percentage, and cent calculation must be rendered with .tabular-numbers and monospace figures to guarantee clean vertical column alignment.

rules.name: The Strictly Flat Rule
rules.body: No ambient blur shadows, fuzzy drop-shadows, or skeuomorphic gradients are permitted on cards or panels. All structural separation is achieved with 1px #E5DDCF borders and #FAF7F2 / #FFFFFF surface shifts. Faint structural 2xs shadows (shadow-2xs) are tolerated only on elevated floating select dropdowns.

dos: Do format all currency and financial totals in monospace tabular figures (font-mono tabular-numbers).
Do use 1px crease borders (#E5DDCF) and paper shifts (#FAF7F2 to #FFFFFF) for spatial depth.
Do reserve Hanko Vermilion (#C53030) strictly for discrepancy alerts and unassigned warnings.
Do ensure all mobile interactive targets maintain at least a 44x44px touch area.
Do celebrate bill balancing with the Matcha Seal (#1B6B38) and verified stamp badges.
donts: Don't use diffuse SaaS drop-shadows or floating multi-layered cards.
Don't introduce generic tech-blue gradients, neon buttons, or purple glow effects.
Don't use proportional fonts for line-item prices, which causes column misalignment.
Don't use low-contrast gray text on prices; money values must remain legible in dim ambient lighting.
Don't clutter the mobile viewport with non-essential decoration during dining table sessions.
